fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Detached Structure; Open Lawn Area; Perimeter Fencing; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can quickly identify the property from the road.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach the front of the residence without delay.
• Trim any shrubs or trees near the residence so responders can move along the exterior walls without obstruction.
• Mark or identify any gate or gap in the perimeter fencing that allows access to the rear of the property.
• Keep any rear gate or fence access point unlocked or secured with a breakaway lock so responders can reach the detached structure without delay.
• Clear a walking path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings quickly.
• Keep the area around the detached structure clear of stored materials or vegetation that would slow responder movement around it.
• Identify the single driveway access point to responding units in advance by registering the property address with your local fire department if a pre-incident survey program is available.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Grass Cover; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Woody Debris
wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove woody debris piles visible near the structure before fire season.
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the structure.
• Thin scattered trees closest to the structure to increase open space between tree canopy and the building.
• Cut or mow dry grass between the scattered shrubs and the structure.
• Remove dead branches and loose woody material from the ground around the structure.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching shrubs so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Separate shrub clusters from one another near the structure so fire cannot move easily from one plant to the next.
• Clear grass and loose debris from underneath any trees near the structure.
• Move any woody debris or cut material away from the structure rather than leaving it in nearby piles.
